folder: Glowrift-Verdana Game UX Project — Pitch Deck
title: Glowrift: imagining a world worth playing
label: Game UX · Team project
short: An action-RPG shaped by player perspectives, from its narrative to its accessibility.
description: An action-RPG concept developed with a five-person team, shaped by concept testing with eight participants and multiple design iterations. This pitch brings together the game’s narrative, player experience, accessibility, and monetization strategy, and was presented to Microsoft and EA representatives for feedback.
question: How can player feedback shape a compelling, accessible game concept?

folder: Glowrift-Verdana Game UX Project — Research & Analysis
title: Behind the world of Glowrift
label: Concept testing · Research
short: Tracing the connection between participant feedback and game design decisions.
description: A closer look at the research behind our action-RPG concept. This deck documents participant feedback and explores how findings informed design decisions across narrative, accessibility, and monetization, connecting player perspectives to the evolution of our game.
question: What changes when we let players help shape the experience?

folder: Community, Co-Presence, and Content Architecture on Bilibili
title: Watching together, alone
label: Information architecture · Course paper
short: Community, co-presence, and the way we discover media on Bilibili.
description: An information architecture analysis exploring how Bilibili organizes content while supporting community and a sense of shared presence. This course paper examines the relationship between platform structure and social experience, considering how content architecture shapes the way people discover and engage with media.
question: How does the structure of a platform create a sense of being together?

folder: Little Nightmares II — Game Experience Analysis
title: Small character. Lasting experience.
label: Game experience · Critical analysis
short: A closer look at how Little Nightmares II creates tension, immersion, and friction.
description: An in-depth analysis of Little Nightmares II through the GUR and GAP categories and concepts studied in class. The paper examines how the game’s design choices shape the player experience, connecting specific examples from gameplay to broader analytical frameworks.
question: How do small design decisions shape the way a game feels?

folder: "Twenty-Four Solar Terms" Life-Simulation Game — Usability Evaluation
title: Making room for a little less friction
label: Usability evaluation · UX internship
short: Evaluating onboarding, quests, navigation, and camera controls in a life-simulation game.
description: A usability evaluation completed during my summer UX design internship, examining onboarding, quest flow, navigation, and camera controls. Through heuristic analysis and gameplay testing, I identified more than 25 issues and proposed design changes grounded in HCI and psychology principles.
question: How can everyday game interactions feel more intuitive?

folder: Furniture Interaction Design — Figma Wireframes & Icon States.jpg
title: A place for everything
label: Interaction design · Figma
short: Wireframes and icon states for a more understandable home-decoration experience.
description: A Figma exploration of home-decoration interactions for a life-simulation game, featuring more than 30 wireframes and UI states. The designs address inventory search, undo and redo, and 3D furniture placement, with icon states that communicate available actions and interaction feedback.
question: How can controls make placing, finding, and adjusting furniture easier to understand?

title: A more accessible way to shop
label: Accessibility · Collaborative audit
short: Identifying barriers and recommending a more inclusive shopping experience.
description: A collaborative accessibility audit of the Urban Outfitters website using both automated and manual testing. Our presentation documents accessibility barriers, explains their impact on users, and recommends changes to make the shopping experience more accessible.
question: What stands between a shopper and an accessible experience?

folder: LLMs, Theory of Mind & Emotional Reasoning
title: Can AI understand how it feels?
label: Human–AI interaction · Independent research
short: Comparing human and model judgments of emotionally difficult social situations.
description: An independent research paper examining how large language models interpret emotionally difficult social situations compared with human judgments. Drawing on 96 human ratings and 80 responses from five LLMs, the study explores social-pain judgments across 16 scenarios and considers their implications for AI’s understanding of human emotional experience.
question: How closely do AI judgments of social pain align with human judgments?
